- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/approvals/requests (route, the route ledger binds it to client method approvals.listRequests))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via listRequests (symbol, a method of class ApprovalService))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via listRequests (symbol, a method of class ApprovalService))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `282e7a68d46e2e0e4676379ff0dea1a7a6073308` — the merge of head `d3ca88e8d36a1fabff23b4dbe9c9284a02f50f5f` into base `8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 282e7a68d46e2e0e4676379ff0dea1a7a6073308 && git checkout 282e7a68d46e2e0e4676379ff0dea1a7a6073308
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294 d3ca88e8d36a1fabff23b4dbe9c9284a02f50f5f && git checkout -B drift-repro 8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294 && git merge --no-ff d3ca88e8d36a1fabff23b4dbe9c9284a02f50f5f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8d05456cbe03667ea2352c9a99e67d4a862a8294` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d3ca88e8d36a1fabff23b4dbe9c9284a02f50f5f`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #23594 (body and all three comments: triage `6184043475`, claim `6184191656`, os-dev-report `6184931715`); PR #23614 body, its 8-file list and the net diff against `main` at the head; the 39 check-runs on the head; `payload-redaction.ts` header on `origin/main` (#10749) and #7497 ruling C (`6051659422`). Function level only, per the card's security gate.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged.**

1. **`record_title` is now picked from the subject record as served to the reader** (`resolveSubjectDisplays`: `redactSnapshot(record, served)` then `pickTitle`), with `served` being `resolveReadableSnapshotFields`' answer asked ONCE per subject object as the reading caller (`servedSubjectFields`). **Right.** This is the #10749 header's rule applied to the title: serve-time, keyed on the reading caller, the same answer the payload snapshot is redacted by (readable intersected with not-masked, #20964). The two narrowings can no longer disagree, and `enrichRows` now requires the map, so no caller can reach the title without stating the narrowing.
2. **Nothing is granted.** **Right.** The subject read itself (`engine.find` under `SYSTEM_CTX`) is unchanged from `main`; what changed is only what is served from that read, and for every reader it is a subset of what was served before. The served set with no field-visibility answer passes through exactly as before; `[]` (the security plugin's fail-closed tier) empties both the snapshot and the title. Record access is untouched: object permissions, sharing and row-level rules decide it as #7497 ruling C keeps them. No route, schema, export, translation key or notification field moves.
3. **The `undefined` posture is the same as the payload redaction's.** **Right, by construction.** Both read one map: `redactPayloads` skips a row whose object answered `undefined`; `resolveSubjectDisplays` uses the whole record for that object; `redactSnapshot(x, undefined)` returns `x` in both. The three fail-open cases of `resolveReadableSnapshotFields` (no security service, no object name, a throwing or `undefined` read projection) and its one fail-closed case (no masked-for-this-caller answer gives `[]`) apply identically to title and snapshot. The production wiring (`approvals-plugin.ts`, lazy `getService('security')`) feeds this single seam, so an absent security plugin serves titles exactly as before, as the changeset says. Map keys match: `servedSubjectFields` keys `String(object_name)` and `enrichRows` groups rows that have a truthy `object_name` string, so no production row misses its answer.
4. **A withheld display field gives no title; a title-eligible field the reader MAY read still names the record** (pin f). **Right under the contract, and a declared narrowing of the card's literal done line.** The value served is one the reader is already served in the snapshot, so nothing the reader may not read ships; this is the rule the pre-existing snapshot fallback (`pickTitle(r.payload, undefined)` over the redacted snapshot) already applied for a deleted subject, and the live pick now matches it. The card's done line reads narrower ("otherwise the reader gets the shape the redaction gives a withheld field"); the PR's choice is named in the changeset and pinned. Accepted; the seat should carry the one-line note on the close.
5. **A display field served MASKED is withheld** (pin a-masked). **Right**: the served set is the read projection intersected with the queryable set, so a masked field is dropped, not reproduced (#20964's reason).
6. **The toast token's source is narrowed.** **Right.** Every request action reads back through `readBackRequest(requestId, context)` under the acting caller, so `result.request.record_title` in the nine `successMessage` strings is the reader's own narrowed row (pin c).
7. **The action-link pages name the record by its id, never the title, for every bearer** (`summaryRows`). **Right as a security posture.** The token chain reads the request under `SYSTEM_CTX` (`resolveActionToken`) and redeems under `SYSTEM_CTX` with the slot's person attached; a system context is not narrowed by field-level security, so the row those pages receive carries the full title and snapshot. The pages render only process, step, record id, object label and requester, and the row is not serialised by any other door (`peekActionToken`/`redeemActionToken` are called only by `handleActionPage` and the self-hosted mount, both HTML). This withholds, it grants nothing. Residual named in ③.
8. **Does any production path still serve a subject title the reader may not read?** On the head I find none. `record_title` is set in exactly one place (`enrichRows`), which is reached only from `listRequests` and `loadRequest`, both of which build the served map from the reader's context first. The REST doors (`rest-server.ts`) pass the caller's context. `nameSubjectRecord` (the `approval.requested` body) carries label and id only. The action-link pages render the id. Two sibling paths outside the card's reach are escalated in ③ (lookup-target titles; the record-lock refusal).
9. **Test accept-set changes.** `action-page-member.integration.test.ts` parity twin: byte equality is kept modulo the one difference the change introduces (each twin's own record id), and each door's page is still pinned equal to the renderer's page for its own request. **Right**: the parity pin is not weakened, its invariant is restated. `payload-display-target-exposure.test.ts` and `implicit-reference-target-lookup.test.ts` pass an empty served map to the private `enrichRows`: the pass-through posture, which is what those pins measure. **Right.** The notification test's comment is corrected, assertions unchanged. **Right.**
10. **New pins** (`subject-title-reader-fls.integration.test.ts`): (a) single and list, (a-masked), (b) deleted subject with snapshot, (c) decision result, (d) both action pages for a restricted bearer and a reader, (e) control, (f) withheld field lends nothing, (g) one ask per object per read. They cover every surface the card's pin names, with the positive control, through the real service on a real engine and a field-visibility source that gives the contract's three answers. Red-before and two restore-proven ablations are reported with predicted and observed sets matching. **Right.** Not measured: a full composition with `plugin-security`; the PR says so.

**Check-runs on the head, as read (latest per name):** 33 completed (28 success, 5 skipped by design: Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood matrix shard, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance). Green: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, every Lint family, every Type Check family, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core (5/6), the claim and single-writer guards. **In progress at read time: Test Core (1/6), (2/6), (3/6), (4/6), (6/6).** None failed. The queue's "every check green" condition is the seat's to read at landing time; this verdict is on the contract.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/23594-subject-title-reader-fls.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` **patch**. **Matches the diff.** The package name matches `package.json`. Nothing published moves: no `packages/spec` file is touched; `ApprovalRequestRow.record_title` is already optional on the contract (`record_title?: string`), so an absent key is within the declared shape; `redactPayloads`, `enrichRows`, `servedSubjectFields` and `resolveSubjectDisplays` are private; `renderConfirmPage`/`renderResultPage` keep their signatures; no route, query parameter or export changes. A narrowing of served values and a page copy change are patch. `skip-changeset` does not apply and was not used.

`Clause-②: no` is on the PR body, the changeset and the claim, and all three agree with the diff: no published schema or public surface is declared or changed. Right.

Governed surfaces: none in the file list (no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `.github/workflows/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`). The Governed Surface Queue Guard is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Open question 1** (a reader whose title is withheld sees the nine success messages render an empty quoted title; A carry, B a server-named always-present display field, C a fallback operator in the action runner's token grammar). **Answered: A, as built.** It leaks nothing (the token reads the reader's own narrowed row), the inbox's inline copy already falls back to the formatted id, and the same shape already toasts for any subject with no resolvable title (920bc12). B adds a second name field to the spec contract beside `record_title`; C is cross-repo grammar growth; neither has a measured producer. The dev named the carrier (objectui#12308, the server-authored-text family card) in `out_of_scope_findings`; the seat carries that note there. Not a reason to fail.

**Open question 2** (the action-link pages withhold the title from every bearer, a reader who could read it included; A keep, B narrow under the token slot's person via a reconstructed grant envelope). **Answered: A.** The page's row is read under the system context, which field-level security cannot narrow, so serving the title there would serve exactly the value this card withholds. B is a second derivation of a person's authorization envelope beside the session's (the shape the seat declined for the notification on #23556), a one-route-one-owner breach with no measured pull. Ruling C's floor for an approver (the inbox entry, the request detail redacted by FLS, and the approve and reject actions) is kept: the pages still decide. **Escalated as a residual for the card close:** the card's positive control ("an approver who can read the field still gets it") holds on the inbox row, request detail and toast, and NOT on the one-tap page, where every bearer now sees the record id. That is a declared narrowing, named in the changeset, not a leak and not a grant.

**Deviation 1** (push order: the pre-fix red run, fix and ablations ran on local commits; one content push carried fix, pins and changeset). Answered: the security rule that nothing red lands on the remote before the fix governs; no contract effect.

**Deviation 2** (four test files beyond the claim's named sources). Answered: all four are tests of the claimed sources, inside the claim's "and their tests"; each is named in the PR body with its reason. Within surface.

**Deviation 3** (model-free commit trailers and the repository's session footer instead of the harness reminder's). Answered: a process note with no contract effect; the repository's instructions govern the seat.

**Out-of-scope notes, each answered or escalated:**
- `nameSubjectRecord`'s inline comment ("withheld until resolveSubjectDisplays narrows it by each reader's FLS") now names a condition this PR meets, while the notification body must stay title-free for want of a reader. Left as the dispatch ruled; **escalated to #23556's remaining half**, which owns that comment and should reword it to the real reason (no per-recipient reader), so the next reader does not read it as a green light.
- `lifecycle-hooks.ts` `recordTitleOf` names the record's title in the RECORD_LOCKED refusal to a WRITER from the engine's update pre-image (`ctx.previous`), which is the raw row inside the engine hook. Unmeasured, outside this card's reach (the writer surface, not the approver's). **Escalated to the seat** to measure whether a writer whose field-level security withholds the display field can be told its value by the refusal, and to file it on its own card if so.
- Assumption 4 (the subject's own declared API exposure does not gate its snapshot or title on the approval path). Answered: consistent with the #10749 header, which says the seam does not gate on object-level access; a design question for a card of its own, correctly not built here.

**One sibling finding of this review (function level, outside the card's scope, no expansion asked):** `enrichRows` still resolves `payload_display` lookup-TARGET titles under `SYSTEM_CTX` and narrows them only by the target object's declared exposure (#22738), not by the reader's field-level security on the TARGET object's display field. The lookup keys themselves come from the already-redacted snapshot, so a withheld lookup field lends nothing, but a readable lookup field's target is titled from the whole target record. This is the same class as #23594 on a referenced record rather than the subject. **Escalated to the seat to file as its own card**; not a defect of this PR, which the card scopes to the subject's `record_title`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23594-subject-title-fls`
Reviewed-by: `session_017WLmd5in9RXu7AjyHR8fKQ`

**VERDICT: PASS**
